transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
Hi Doctor. I'm hoping to get some help because I've been struggling a lot with staying focused and making careless mistakes with details. I also find it really hard to finish tasks and often
Have these problems with focus and finishing tasks been present since childhood, such as in school, or did they start more recently?

Yes, these issues actually go all the way back to my childhood, definitely before I was 12 years old. I remember struggling with schoolwork even back then, and it has been a constant, frustrating struggle that's been especially bad for the last two years.
Along with the focus problems, do you also often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble staying seated, or act or speak impulsively?

Yes, I definitely feel a constant sense of restlessness, like I'm always on the go and can't quite settle down. It is really hard to just sit still because of that internal jittery feeling. I'm not really sure about the impulsive part, though.
Do you also often talk more than other people, interrupt or blurt things out, or have trouble waiting your turn?
No, I wouldn't say I have those issues. I don't really struggle with talking too much, interrupting others, or waiting my turn. I'm actually usually on the quieter side in conversations.
Do you often find yourself unable to relax quietly, or feel driven to keep moving or doing things even when you want to slow down?

Yes, definitely. I find it really hard to just relax quietly, and I almost always feel this inner drive to keep moving or doing something. Even when I'm supposed to be resting, I just can't seem to shake that restless feeling.
Do you often lose things, get easily distracted, forget daily tasks or appointments, or avoid tasks that need a lot of sustained mental effort?

No, I don't really struggle with those specific issues. I'm actually pretty good at keeping track of my things and remembering appointments, and I don't usually avoid tasks just because they require a lot of mental effort.
As a child, did teachers or family often notice that you were running around, climbing, leaving your seat, or seeming constantly on the go?

Yes, they definitely did. Before I was 12, my teachers and family members were always pointing out that I was constantly running around, climbing on things inappropriately, and just couldn't stay seated or still.
Do these restlessness and activity-level problems currently cause significant trouble at work, school, or in relationships?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about my restlessness causing specific problems in my work or relationships in that way.
Can you think of any recent times when your restlessness or difficulty staying still led to problems at work, school, or with other people?

Yes, I frequently experience a strong sense of inner restlessness that makes it incredibly hard to stay still. During long meetings at work, I find sitting so uncomfortable that I constantly fidget or find excuses to stand up and pace. This has actually caused some issues because my colleagues and boss have told me it makes me look distracted or impatient.
Besides trouble focusing and finishing tasks, do you often have trouble organizing tasks, following through on instructions, or seem not to listen when people speak to you directly?

Yes, I definitely have a lot of trouble following through on instructions and actually finishing my chores or work duties. I'm not as sure about having trouble organizing tasks or not listening when spoken to, but that difficulty with following through is a major issue for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports both inattentive symptoms and hyperactive symptoms beginning before age 12 and persisting into adulthood, with current impairment at work. Inattention is supported by difficulty sustaining focus, careless mistakes, trouble finishing tasks, and difficulty following through on instructions. Hyperactivity is supported by chronic restlessness, inability to sit still or relax quietly, feeling driven to keep moving, and childhood reports of running/climbing and leaving seat. Because clinically significant symptoms are present in both domains, Combined Presentation is most consistent.
